reference: Why can you untangle a friend's problem faster than your own? Researchers call it Solomon's paradox. Across three experiments, people reasoned more wisely about someone else's conflict than their own. But when they reflected from a distance, the gap disappeared. Self-talk using your own name also led to better speeches and less distress. So when you're stuck, ask yourself by name: Alex, what would you tell a friend? Take a mindful break with Mello.
